The (In,Ga)As cores were grown at a high temperature of around 500°C, while the (Ga,Mn)As shells were deposited at a much lower temperature of around 220°C.
Both the (In,Ga)As cores and the (Ga,Mn)As shells have a wurtzite crystal structure, which is different from the typical zinc-blende structure observed in planar (III,Mn)-V layers.
The Raman scattering data indicates that the In content in the (In,Ga)As cores is around 12 ± 4%.
The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analysis confirmed the presence of 5 ± 0.5% Mn in the (Ga,Mn)As shells.
The (Ga,Mn)As shells exhibit ferromagnetic coupling at temperatures above 33 K, but the overall magnetic behavior is superparamagnetic.
Two different methods were used to extract the nanowires from the growth substrate and transfer them onto a new support for magnetic measurements.
The growth rate of the nanowires is observed to be almost 5 times faster than that of the planar layers grown with the same III and V element fluxes, reaching around 1 μm/h.
The density of the nanowires on the substrate is high, around 2 x 10^9 nanowires/cm^2.
The core-shell structure allows for the incorporation of a high Mn content in the (Ga,Mn)As shells, which is not possible in the nanowires grown at high temperatures.
The ability to grow (In,Ga)As and (Ga,Mn)As in the wurtzite structure allows for the fabrication of new types of heterostructures that are not achievable in the traditional zinc-blende geometry.
The (Ga,Mn)As shells contain a sizable hole concentration, estimated to be around 3 x 10^19 cm^-3 based on the Raman scattering data.
The (In,Ga)As cores and (Ga,Mn)As shells have a sharp and coherent interface, with no misfit dislocations observed.
The (Ga,Mn)As shells deposited on the gold catalyst at the top of the nanowires are polycrystalline and of irregular shape.
Basal stacking faults were found in the top parts of some of the nanowires, but the majority of the nanowires have a low density of structural defects.
The (Ga,Mn)As layer deposited in between the nanowires has a thickness of up to 70 nm, which can contribute to the measured magnetic signal.
